page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highmem-2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 2 vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture, it provides 1 physical core with 2 threads. The CPU allocation is dedicated, supported by a cache hierarchy of 32 KB L1d, 0.5 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. The instance does not include bundled local storage or GPUs, and comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance is limited, scoring in the bottom 25% for both stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core tests due to the low core count. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with small-block read-only cached bandwidth in the bottom 10% and large-block read/write bandwidth in the bottom 25%. Text processing, single-threaded gzip compression, and small-model LLM text generation perform at average levels, while database operations, Redis SET operations, and software compilation fall into the bottom 10% of tested systems.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c2d-highmem-2 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per vCPU, making it a viable entry-level option for workloads requiring more memory than compute power without paying for unnecessary CPU cores. Given its strong single-core performance but weak multi-core and database execution metrics, this instance is best suited for lightweight single-threaded applications, basic text processing, simple web serving, and memory-bound tasks that do not require high parallel processing or intensive disk I/O.
